title: Webinar: The State Of China Tech
gist: Paywalled teaser for a Gavekal webinar (Arthur Kroeber, Laila Khawaja, AJ Cortese) timed to the Trump-Xi meeting in Washington, framing the near-term China tech questions as how close Chinese AI labs are to US frontier models and whether the two sides can begin negotiating AI-safety rules. The deeper framing is the overall US-China balance of technological power and how far the two can actually unwind their thick tech interdependence; no findings or data are disclosed in the accessible text.

insights.claim: Gavekal frames the Donald Trump-Xi Jinping meeting in Washington (September 2026) as an event that puts China's fast-growing technology capabilities at the center of the US-China agenda.
insights.speaker: Gavekal Research
insights.so_what: Treat summit headlines as a potential catalyst for China-tech and AI-related equities and for export-control expectations; watch communiqué language on technology.

themes.theme: Chinese AI labs vs US frontier models

insights.claim: Gavekal identifies the gap between Chinese artificial-intelligence labs and US frontier models as one of the two big open questions in US-China tech, implying the gap is narrow enough to be actively debated rather than assumed large.
insights.speaker: Gavekal Research
insights.so_what: If Chinese labs are near parity, the pricing power and moat assumptions behind US frontier-model leaders deserve scrutiny; track benchmark and cost comparisons.
insights.quote: how close Chinese artificial-intelligence labs are to matching the US frontier models
insights.locator: Intro: the big questions at the moment

insights.claim: Gavekal raises as a live question whether the US and China can start negotiating rules on AI safety, positioning bilateral AI governance talks as a possible outcome of summit-level diplomacy.
insights.speaker: Gavekal Research
insights.so_what: Any start of US-China AI-safety negotiations would signal a thaw that could soften tech-war tail risk; absence of it keeps decoupling risk premia intact.
insights.quote: whether the two sides can start negotiating rules on AI safety
insights.locator: Intro: the big questions at the moment

insights.claim: Gavekal argues that beneath the AI-parity and AI-safety debates sit bigger structural questions: the overall balance of technological power between the US and China, and how far the two tech powers can actually unwind the thick webs of interdependence that bind them.
insights.speaker: Gavekal Research
insights.so_what: Frame China-tech exposure around the degree of feasible decoupling, not headline rhetoric; businesses embedded in cross-border tech supply chains carry the most two-way risk.
insights.quote: how far can the world's two big tech powers go in pulling apart the thick webs of interdependence that tie them together?
